page:
Using DevEnvironment class instances in Vite. Environment API release candidate: experimental features subject to change. Multi-environment dev server with separate module graphs.
- DevEnvironment class: represents each environment during dev
- name: unique identifier per dev server ('client' default, 'ssr' optional)
- hot: NormalizedHotChannel for communication with module runner
- moduleGraph: EnvironmentModuleGraph with import relationships
- plugins: resolved plugins including per-environment created plugins
- pluginContainer: environment plugins pipeline for resolve/load/transform
- config: ResolvedConfig + ResolvedDevEnvironmentOptions for environment
- transformRequest(url): resolve, load, transform URL through plugins
- Returns: TransformResult with code, map, etag, deps, dynamicDeps
- warmupRequest(url): pre-transform frequently used files (avoid waterfalls)
- fetchModule(id, importer?, options?): retrieve module info for module runner
- Internal use only (not for manual calling)
- Returns: FetchResult (union of CachedFetchResult, ExternalFetchResult, ViteFetchResult)
- server.environments: access environments in dev
- server.environments.client: client environment
- server.environments.ssr: SSR environment
- DevEnvironmentContext: hot (boolean), transport, options, remoteRunner, depsOptimizer
- TransformResult: code, map (SourceMap or empty mappings), etag, deps, dynamicDeps
- EnvironmentModuleNode: module representation with id, url, file, type, importers, importedModules
- importedBindings: Map<string, Set<string>> for imported bindings
- info, meta: ModuleInfo and metadata
- transformResult: cached transform result
- acceptedHmrDeps, acceptedHmrExports: HMR state
- EnvironmentModuleGraph: module graph with urlToModuleMap, idToModuleMap, etagToModuleMap, fileToModulesMap
- getModuleByUrl, getModuleById, getModulesByFile: retrieve modules
- onFileChange, onFileDelete: invalidate modules
- invalidateModule, invalidateAll: invalidation methods
- ensureEntryFromUrl, createFileOnlyEntry: module creation
- resolveUrl: resolve raw URL to full URL
- updateModuleTransformResult: cache transform result
- getModuleByEtag: retrieve by etag
- CachedFetchResult: cache confirmation (cache: true)
- ExternalFetchResult: externalized module (externalize: file://, type: 'module'/'commonjs'/'builtin'/'network')
- ViteFetchResult: module code and metadata
- code: string for evaluation
- file: file path on disk (null for virtual modules)
- id: module ID in server graph
- url: module URL used in import
- invalidate: boolean for client-side cache invalidation

sections.manifest:
Accessing environments in dev server.
- server.environments: object with available environments
- server.environments.client: client environment instance
- server.environments.ssr: SSR environment instance (if configured)
- From plugins: current environment via plugin hooks
- methods: transformRequest, warmupRequest, fetchModule
- properties: moduleGraph for module graph operations
How do I access environments?

DevEnvironment class interface.
- name: unique environment identifier ('client', 'ssr', custom names)
- hot: NormalizedHotChannel for module runner communication
- moduleGraph: EnvironmentModuleGraph with module relationships
- plugins: resolved plugins (including per-environment)
- pluginContainer: plugins pipeline for resolve/load/transform
- config: ResolvedConfig + environment-specific options
- constructor: DevEnvironment(name, config, context)
- transformRequest(url, options?): process and cache module
- warmupRequest(url): pre-process for performance
- fetchModule(id, importer?, options?): get module for runner (internal use)
What's in the DevEnvironment class?

Separate module graphs per environment.
- Each environment: isolated module graph
- Same signature: generic algorithms work across graphs
- hotUpdate example: file modification triggers HMR per environment
- Vite 5: mixed client and SSR graph
- Old properties: clientImportedModules, ssrImportedModules, importedModules union
- Backward compatibility layer: ecosystem migration support
- Module nodes: EnvironmentModuleNode per environment
Why are module graphs separate?

EnvironmentModuleNode structure.
- environment: environment name
- url: module URL
- id: module ID (null initially)
- file: file path (null for virtual modules)
- type: 'js' or 'css'
- importers: Set of importer modules
- importedModules: Set of imported modules
- importedBindings: Map<string, Set<string>> of named bindings
- info: ModuleInfo metadata
- meta: custom metadata Record
- transformResult: cached TransformResult (null initially)
- acceptedHmrDeps: Set of HMR boundary modules
- acceptedHmrExports: Set of accepted exports (null = all)
- isSelfAccepting: boolean flag
- lastHMRTimestamp, lastInvalidationTimestamp: timestamps
What does EnvironmentModuleNode contain?

EnvironmentModuleGraph methods.
- urlToModuleMap, idToModuleMap, etagToModuleMap, fileToModulesMap: internal maps
- getModuleByUrl(rawUrl): retrieve module by URL
- getModuleById(id): retrieve module by ID
- getModulesByFile(file): retrieve all modules for file
- onFileChange(file): invalidate modules for file
- onFileDelete(file): handle file deletion
- invalidateModule(mod, seen?, timestamp?, isHmr?): invalidate single module
- invalidateAll(): invalidate entire graph
- ensureEntryFromUrl(rawUrl, setIsSelfAccepting?): get or create entry
- createFileOnlyEntry(file): create entry for file
- resolveUrl(url): resolve URL to ResolvedUrl
- updateModuleTransformResult(mod, result): cache transform result
- getModuleByEtag(etag): retrieve by etag
What methods does EnvironmentModuleGraph provide?

FetchResult types for module runner.
- Union of CachedFetchResult, ExternalFetchResult, ViteFetchResult
- CachedFetchResult: cache: true (module cached, not invalidated)
- ExternalFetchResult: externalize module via runExternalModule
- externalize: file:// path for native import
- type: 'module', 'commonjs', 'builtin', 'network' (determine import correctness)
- ViteFetchResult: module code for execution
- code: string to evaluate (wrapped in async function)
- file: file path on disk (null for virtual modules, used for import.meta.url)
- id: module ID in server graph
- url: module URL from import statement
- invalidate: boolean (true for HMR updates, skip cache)
